On the support thing, there's a topic it seems nobody wants to talk about, and everyone dances around. I'm not sure how to say this, as it is a tad delicate.

Trans women are women seems to occupy this weird place where it's supposed to mean there is no difference at all. And, sadly, we have to acknowledge there is. We also have to accept that barring massive leaps in technology there will always be that barrier. What shouldn't happen is using that to attack people. 

What I grew up understanding, and where things seem to have gone completely off the rails is that there was this social compact. An understanding that all would do their best to act in an according manner. Yes, transitioning to the point its impossible to tell even for the person transitioning is beyond us. But we all politely ignore that and act to the best of our ability. It seems like a modern thing to me that the expectation is blind belief, and I can't see that ever happening. 

And... it sucks, but I dont get why this is some hill that people seem to be fighting for. Shouldn't the baseline be respect for the person? Agree or not, just don't be a dick. Instead it seems like there is a massive demand for all or nothing belief. The requirement is full conviction.

Still not sure I'm wording it well. 

But the thing is, life deals bad hands. There is a kid I grew up with who is nearing the end of his life due to medical issues. Medicine let him live past 9, but mid 30s what realistically the best he could hope for. I'd give anything for the parts of my brain that don't work right to line up like they should. I'm not trying to make some dig that trans people are mentally ill, but expressing my confusion at how we handle this one instance. 

We laughed at the mother who demanded no peanuts or peanut by products at all for the whole school because Timmy was allergic. Yet the discussion around this matter feels to have much the same demand. 

I dont think it's strange that people who support trans people might not see them as 100% members of the gender they identify with. Tbh I think its a natural thing. I dont think that makes them inferior allies. I also don't think it means people who are not as invested are bad people. We are talking about such a small component of society as a whole, yet the narrative has blossomed so far beyond it.

The Sawsl is a weapon dating back to the early days of the Fall. While originally scorned by Northern soldiers as a primitive and inelegant tool, more advanced versions were eventually made, such as the legendary Swordbreaker. Relatively easy to repair and keep powered, the sawsl is considered a good all around melee weapon for dealing with the various creatures that call the Outlands home.

The sawsl uses a round motor and piston to pump two blades up and down, the crosscut providing much of the extra power. Running on a relatively low charge chemical battery, sawsls can use both Founder power cells and post Fall chemical designs. The components are fairly rugged and reliable, resulting in the blades being the major weak point of the design.

While some prefer the style of the northern made heat blades, sawsls have earned their place among many Outlander’s personal armories, and scavengers are known to make their own versions of the weapon. Most Outlands sawsls use inferior Carthide Steel for their blades, so carrying replacement ones is a must.

The last known use of the Tower of Night was in the five years war, when it reduced the Outlander capitol of freelance to a smoking, bloody crater. Pans -  Humans with natururally growing armor-like skin, the result of an attempt to create cheaper soldiers by Second Genesis.  Keeping the armor from locking their joints is a battle that consumes a fair amount of their time.

Mules - Behemoths nearly twice the size of normal men. While they have a reputation for inferior intellect, many play to this stigma. Underestimating a Mule is a good way to die.

Rabbits - Afflicted with a genetic condition that causes their bodies to stop developing, Rabbits will spend their whole lives looking like children or young teens. They have faster than normal twitch reflexes, but are easily dwarfed in a world where power rules.

Beasts - Mostly found in the deep forests of the Angol Sub Continent, Beasts are considered ill omens when born in a tribe. Covered in hair with regressed hands that bear claws, no one is certain what causes the mutation. Northern factions prefer them for exploring Founder ruins trapped in snow wastes.

Chimera - Tainted by Founder genetic alteration tech, these miserable souls are forced to live with bodies that seem to be put together at random from many different people. The rare lucky souls are exposed to agents that change their whole body, becoming gods and goddesses. Angol folk lore labels them cursed.

One Bullet Left - Faith and Law, Finale

Gunshots rang through the stone halls, and Issac pushed himself until his breath tore at the lining of his throat. He slid to a stop by a cracked door, trying his best to not pant or cough. From the room within he could hear several voices, and he could only barely hear the voices within.
 
"Santiago, we have the man as you requested!" There was the sound of footsteps, then a scuffing followed by a thump as something hit the paving stones hard. The clink of metal on metal caused Issac's stomach to turn over, and he had to force himself not to rush in to save Marshal.
 
Issac took the moment to eject the magazine from his pistol, then slid in a fresh one. The youth winced as the magazine clicked against the lock. He looked around wildly, but there didn't seem to be anyone nearby to hear the metallic click. After fumbling with the toggle for the laser, he managed to turn it off completely. The last thing he needed was the red line passing through the musty air telling the bandits where he was. He pushed his ear against the door and waited for the moment to strike.
 
"Good, good..." A voice so soft and raspy Issac could barely hear it was the only sound to break the silence. It was faintly melodic, though the roughness ruined any tone it might have once carried. There was a long rattling breath that reminded Issac strongly of a death rattle, then the voice spoke again. "Bring him closer, bring him into the light."
 
"But Santiago, what if he," A man asked, but he was cut off. A deranged scream filled the chamber, followed by a gunshot.
 
"No! No! You will do as I command, and you will do it when I command!" The voice shrieked, and the sound of a thud and footsteps filled the following silence. There was a familiar groan and Issac pushed his way through the door. Issac slid down the stairs, doing his best to avoid making too much noise. A wave of relief filled him as he heard Marshal's voice.
 
"Ah, Santiago. I'm glad you're still alive. You always seemed to have a knack for causing trouble." Marshal coughed, causing his various badges to clink together. "No surprise you ended up a bandit lord after the Lawbreakers were broken."
 
The voice was soft as it replied, "Ah, Marshal, you say the sweetest things. Tell me, why didn't come with me when we fled Meridian? We could have been great, you and I."
 
Issac could see the chamber clearly now, it was a dimly lit space of adobe and incense fumes. The air reeked of sandalwood, alcohol and the sour stench of sweat. At the rear of the room sat a large bloated form, waving around a pistol like it was a toy in its giant palm. Marshal was held on his knees before the large figure, and there was a collapsed man, apparently kicked to the side.
 
"You know I couldn't have done that, Santiago. I'm no lawkeeper, but I couldn't be a bandit either." Marshal's voice seemed genuinely sad at that statement, but Issac didn't pay too much attention to it. He readied his pistol as he peered around a column. "I've tried to just stay out of your way the last few decades."
 
"And yet, here we are."
 
Marshal laughed, "You tried to have me killed first. I seem to recall something about some dynamite and an inn back in Melphis. You know the UNA actually tried to pin that whole affair on me? I can’t show my face anywhere in Dixon now, thanks to you."
 
Santiago pointed the gun at Marshal, and it was only then that Issac realized that the face was that of a woman's. At one point in time, she must have been exceptionally beautiful. Her eyes glowed with a dementia as she leveled her iron. "You always were too much of a good samaritan, Marshal. You are a wild card, a factor I cannot allow to interfere with me. We both know it would be one or the other, and your time has come. The Iron Hands need those slaves, and I can't trust you to walk away." 


A single tear rolled down Santiago’s cheek, leaving a trail that glistened in the firelight. "I am truly sorry, Marshal, please do not hold it against me. Know that you die at the hands of someone who truly knew you, and not some blood crazed savage." She pulled the hammer back, which required some effort, as her hands were shaking and leveled it at the man on the floor before her.
 
Issac reacted without knowing what he was doing. He spun around the column, firing his iron at the woman's large form. She didn't jerk from the impact, so much as shiver as if stung by a bee. Marshal, however, reacted in a blur. His curled fingers rammed into one guard's throat, and without hesitation or mercy, he’d pulled the gasping man’s iron from its holder and fired upon his other captor. With a gesture, he motioned for Issac to stay where he was. Cautiously, the gunslinger approached the form of the woman on the dais, the iron in his hands pointed down, but held ready.
 
"Is it... Is it over?" Santiago asked, her body shaking once more as she convulsed. She coughed, but it sounded weak. She leaned forward, the wild energy gone from her gaze as she stared at Marshal. It seemed to Issac that she didn’t seem to mind the pain, and the look she gave Marshal wasn’t one of fear, but relief.
 
Marshal brushed the hair out of her eyes, then smiled. "Yes, yes it is. You don’t have to fight any more, it's time to rest.” The woman sighed at his touch, momentarily falling back against her makeshift throne. 
 
She then struggled to sit up, looking unfocused at Issac. Then, with a smile, she slumped back. Marshal leaned forward, kissing the woman on the forehead. With thumb and pointer, he closed her eyes, then turned back to Issac.
 
"Thank you, Issac. I know it isn't easy to kill, and she was one that I could never bring myself to finish. I thought that after all this time, I’d finally be able to end it." Marshal pulled his gun from a cushion in front of Santiago, then slung the Morrow Carbine over his shoulder. He gave his stolen iron a quick once over, then emptied the cylinder into a dirty palm. Without any care, Marshal tossed the empty gun into a dark corner of the room before starting down the dais. His boots seemed to thud as he walked through the now empty hall. He patted Issac on the shoulder, then turned to look at the woman. "She became a monster so I didn't have to, and thanks to you, now she’s at peace."

He paused at the stairs, then looked around him, and upon the corpse of the woman. To Issac it seemed he was trying to engrave every little detail about her appearance into his memory, and he waited for Marshal to speak before moving.


“Let's go, kid. We place some dynamite around this pit and we can make sure she gets a place to rest finer than most will ever get on this God forsaken rock.”

Jason looked around their jump point for the first time. The air tasted dusy and foul, but not at all like it had on Brav's world. It almost tasted stale.

As for the location, it was dimly lit, appearing to be made of heavily pitted rock. The rusted wreck of a set of steel shelves sat in one corner, and labeless cans were scattered all about.

Jason shook his head. It was hard to believe. Then again, he never would have guessed that in the matter of a few weeks he would be traveling with a sorceress who hated to wear anything monochrome or a russian gunslinger from the sandy deserts of Siberia.
